newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Mining says prosecutors raid office. [CORRECTED 04:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Mining says prosecutors raid office. [CORRECTED 04:20 GMT]

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors raided the offices of Mitsui Mining Co Ltd on Friday in connection with a probe into alleged tax evasion by an Osaka-based oil dealer, a Mitsui spokesman said.
The move follows on the heels of Thursday's raid by prosecutors of Mitsubishi Oil Co's Tokyo headquarters in the same case.
Mitsui Mining and Mitsubishi Oil are widely reported to have had transactions with Junichi Izui, a domestic oil products trader arrested on Thursday on suspicion of tax evasion.

Mitsubishi Oil Managing Director (Corrects from President) Masayuki Matsushita, in a Thursday news conference, denied his company had direct ties to Izui or that it had entered into unusual oil deals with him.

The Mitsui Mining spokesman declined to comment further on the case, although he said it may be discussed at a previously scheduled news conference due at 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), when the company will announce its earnings results for the April-September half year.
Sources close to the Osaka Taxation Bureau said last week that Izui was suspected of evading 320 million yen in taxes from 1992 to 1994.

According to documents submitted in a legal dispute between the two energy companies, Mitsui Mining said Mitsubishi Oil paid 2.4 billion yen to Izui in oil deals from 1993 to 1995. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-5473-3708
